text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening stance against driverless cars","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a definite position right away and tells the reader exactly what the essay will argue."},{"evidence":"argument that driverless cars are \"not as reliable\" and could \"ultimately cause more crashes\"","quality":"central claim development","description":"It builds a focused main argument that stays consistent across the essay."},{"evidence":"\"What happens when there is such a big issue that the car can't handle it on their own?\"","quality":"reasoning depth","description":"It explains why the position matters by pushing its claims into specific consequences and counter-scenarios."},{"evidence":"\"car accidents would become way more frequent\" and \"death and economic issues\"","quality":"conclusion of consequences","description":"It connects the argument to broader outcomes instead of ending with only a general opinion."},{"evidence":"\"What about if the system glitches\" and \"The driver wouldn't be paying attention\"","quality":"counterargument anticipation","description":"It anticipates failure cases and responds to the likely objection that automation would still be convenient."}]}
